title: fix(plugin-auth): an organization-delete read that fails refuses 503 before better-auth's first write
body:
Fixes #25059

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

Why `Clause-②: no`: the refusal replaces an outcome only a failed store read produces, and the typed 503 replaces a bare 500 fault; no request a caller can make is answered differently.

## What changed

`AuthManager.assertOrganizationDeletable`, the `POST /organization/delete` admission in better-auth's global `hooks.before`:

- **A failed session read refuses as well.** `resolveActor` answered a failed session read with `null`, the value "no session" gives, so the admission fell through. It takes an opt-in `failedReadThrows` option now. With it, when no actor was resolved and the explicit token read itself threw, that throw propagates, and the admission answers it with the same typed `503`. No credential, a credential the store does not hold, an expired session, a credential that does not parse, and one carrying a control character all still answer `null`, so they reach better-auth's `401`. Only the admission passes the option. The other nine `this.resolveActor(ctx)` call sites are byte-identical in the diff.
- **A read it decides on that fails now refuses.** A failed read of the caller's `sys_member` row or of the `sys_organization` row used to land in `catch { return; }` and hand the request to better-auth, which re-reads, then clears the session's active organization, then deletes the members and invitations, and only then meets the engine's refusal at the organization row. It now answers `503` with the standard ADR-0112 code `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, before better-auth's first write.
- **A failed Default Organization decision answers the same typed `503`.** It already refused before any write, but with a bare `Error`, which better-auth serves as an untyped 500.
- **The vendor-decided cases still fall through, unchanged:** no actor, no member row, not permitted, no organization row.
- The wire pieces sit beside the 409's in `organization-delete.ts`: `ORGANIZATION_DELETE_READ_FAULT_CODE` and `organizationDeleteReadFaultBody(object)`. The body names the table it could not read. The driver's own error rides `cause` and is not relayed. Two names were added to the existing `organization-delete.js` import list in `auth-manager.ts`; nothing else outside the method moved.

## The four mechanism assumptions, re-measured on this branch

1. **The lookup block.** Measured: it holds four lookups, but `resolveActor` cannot throw. Both of its paths catch, and it answers `null`, the same value as "no session". So of the four, three can throw into the catch: the `sys_member` read, `hasPermission` and the `sys_organization` read.
2. **The Default Organization decision answers 500.** Measured by ablation A2 below: with this change reverted to main's bare propagation, the pin reads `expected 500 to be 503`.
3. **Which status and code.** `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`: the vocabulary this file already uses for a read fault (the organization slug guard, the invitation role cap and the invitation placement check), a `StandardErrorCode`, so the error-code ledger needs no row. `check:dispatcher-error-vocabulary` ran green (Verification below).
4. **Can `hasPermission` throw for a decidable vendor answer?** Yes, and only for that. better-auth 1.7.12 `plugins/organization/has-permission.mjs` reaches the adapter only behind `options.dynamicAccessControl?.enabled`, and the admission hands it the roles map alone, so the call reads nothing. It throws only on the member row itself: a role that is not a string (`role.split`), or a role name that resolves to an inherited object member (`authorize` is not a function). better-auth's `deleteOrganization` calls the identical predicate (the same roles object: `organizationOptions.roles` is the `customOrgRoles` the admission holds as `orgRolesMap`) on the same row, before `setActiveOrganization`. So that throw keeps falling through, and a pin holds that nothing is attempted when it does.

## The session read

The card names `resolveActor` among the lookups that throw. Measured: it never threw. Both of its paths catch and answer `null`, so a failed session read read as "no actor" and fell through. An uncommitted scratch test failed only the admission's own session reads while better-auth's stayed real; it got `200`, and better-auth's session update and member and organization deletes ran with nothing counted.

`resolveActor(ctx, { failedReadThrows: true })` now tells the two apart. It is used by the admission alone, and the default reading is unchanged for the other nine callers.

Only the explicit token read counts as a failed read. Two things are deliberately not counted:
- the first path's throw, when the second path finds no token;
- a failure reading a token that carries a control character. PostgreSQL refuses U+0000 in a text parameter, and a crafted cookie can carry `%00`. Counting it would turn that request's `401` into a `503`.

## Pins

`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete-read-fault.test.ts`. Real `ObjectQL` over `@objectstack/driver-sql` and better-sqlite3, the manifest's objects, a real `AuthManager` with the organization plugin (the `session-read-failure-answer.test.ts` harness).

- **One case per read that can fail:** the caller's session read (both of `resolveActor`'s paths fail inside the admission's call, fired 2), the caller's `sys_member` read, the `sys_organization` read, and the Default Organization decision's count. The admission's own read fails once, scoped to the admission's frame, so better-auth's reads of the same table stay real. Each case asserts `503`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` and the table named. It also asserts that no write was attempted: the session update and the member, invitation and organization deletes are recorded by engine hooks when attempted, not when committed. Then a CONTROL: with the read back, the same delete answers `200` and the organization is gone.
- **What still falls through:** a request with no session gets better-auth's `401`, with nothing attempted. A credential carrying a control character gets the same `401`, with nothing attempted, even while the admission's read of it fails.
- **The `hasPermission` fall-through:** a stored member row whose role is null reaches better-auth, which refuses before its first write. Nothing is attempted, and the answer is not the admission's `503`.

### Ablations

A1 to A3 ran at `947ab6c25` (before the merge of `main`); A4 and A5 at `5884148db`, the final head (baseline there `Tests 7 passed (7)`). The test imports `./auth-manager.js` relatively, so the subject resolves to `src/` and no build sits between a mutation and its run. Each mutation was applied with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the anchor hit once, landed on disk, blob changed), and then restored.

| | mutation | result |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | none | `Tests 4 passed (4)` |
| A1 | the read helper swallows the fault (main's fall-through put back) | the three read pins red, each `expected 200 to be 503`: the request reached better-auth and deleted the organization |
| A2 | the Default Organization decision propagates bare (main's R3) | its pin red, `expected 500 to be 503`; the other three green |
| A3 | a `hasPermission` throw refuses `503` instead of falling through | the fall-through pin red, `expected '{"code":"SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE",…' not to contain 'SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE'` |
| A4 | `resolveActor` swallows the failed session read again | the session-read pin red, `expected 200 to be 503`: the request reached better-auth and deleted the organization |
| A5 | the control-character guard removed | the control-character pin red, `expected 503 to be 401` |

Restore after each mutation: blob `f3015ed6f7b0` == HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, zero markers on disk, `git status --porcelain` empty.

## Verification

- At the final head `5884148db`, under the lock: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth build` exit 0; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run` gave `Test Files 185 passed (185)`, `Tests 3485 passed | 10 skipped (3495)`; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK`, no debt row added); `pnpm check:type-check-debt` exit 0 (`re-measure: OK — 1 ledger entr(ies) re-measured in 190.9s, 26 raw tsc error(s) total, none above its recorded number`). The lock printed `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
- Gate union at `5884148db`: the 70 commands derived by `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (the same 70 at `947ab6c25`, `46c61dade` and `5884148db`), plus `check-changeset-fixed` and `check:authz-resolver`, whose rosters sit in a directory this diff touches. Every exit code was captured before any pipe, and all are 0. `--ran`: `70 derived · 70 run · 0 NOT-MEASURED · 0 UNRUN`.
- The other nine callers: in the diff, the one changed `resolveActor(` line is the admission's; `git grep` counts nine `this.resolveActor(ctx)` call sites, and `failedReadThrows: true` occurs once (`auth-manager.ts:8378`, inside `assertOrganizationDeletable`).
- Not run locally: the full-farm `check:*` sweep, `pnpm lint`, the dogfood battery (the title carries no `!` and there is no `(narrowing)` arm), and the `packages/qa` dogfood pins. CI runs those; every check-run on `5884148db` succeeded or was skipped.

## Acceptance notes

- The #24948 dogfood pin for a failed Default Organization lookup (`packages/qa/dogfood/test/organization-delete-federated-fixture.dogfood.test.ts:282`) asserts a status of 400 or above. It stays green with `503`. It could be tightened to `503` plus `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`. That file is in the `domain:cli` lane and was not edited here.
- The record count (`organizationDeleteRefusal` / `defaultOrganizationDeleteRefusal`) still propagates a failure bare, as an untyped 500. That is the same family as the Default Organization decision. It is not changed here because what reaches it is not only a store fault: an engine refusal carrying its own code lands there too, so a blanket `503` would mislabel it.
- A client sees `503 SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` from an organization delete only when a store read failed. Nothing was deleted then, and a retry is the remedy.
